full_judgment:
Mahmudul Hoque J: This Rule Nisi was issued under Article 102 of the Constitution of Bangladesh at the instance of the petitioner calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Judgment and Order dated 9-4-1996 passed by the First Court of Settlement (i.e. the respondent No. 2) in Settlement Court Case No. 17 of 1990 should not be declared illegal, void and passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule Nisi in brief are that the holding No. VII/4, Salimullah Road (formerly known as Quaid-e-Azam Road), Block-"D", Police Station-Mohammadpur, Dhaka-1207, comprising an area of 144 square yards having two-storied building originally belonged to one Mojibur Rahman Khan through a deed of perpetual lease being No. 10007 dated 29-7-1960. He transferred the property to the petitioner by a registered deed of sale being No. 3041 dated 25-8-1983 in pursuance of an agreement of sale of the year 1970 and the possession of the property was handed over to the petitioner. Since then the petitioner has been owning and possessing the case property peacefully and without any interference from any quarter and within the knowledge of all concerned.

3. The original lessee Mojibur Rahman Khan mortgaged the case property with the House Building Finance Corporation, Dhaka as security against loan taken for the purpose of construction of two-storied building thereon and the lessee thereby constructed a two-storied building on the case land.

4. The lessee executed a General Power of Attorney in favour of one Mr PC Barua on 20-5-1972 for looking after the case property and the said General Power of Attorney was subsequently cancelled by the lessee through a Deed of Revocation executed and registered on 25-8-1983 and the same had been communicated to the said Mr PC Barua. Since then the petitioner has been looking after the case property and let out some portion of the case building to the tenants who paid monthly rents to the petitioner. There after the petitioner requested his tenants to vacate the house but they instead of vacating the premises instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 12 of 1985 for specific performance of contract in respect of the said case property on the basis of a fictitious deed of agreement with a view to grab the suit property and the suit was filed against the Attorney of the petitioner's vendor. After coming to know about the case of his tenant named Sudatta Kumar Barua the petitioner got added as a defendant in the suit and filed written statement but the plaintiff discontinued the suit reflected in an order of dismissal for non-prosecution.

5. It is further stated that after registration of the deed of sale in favour of the petitioner by the vendor in the year 1983 the petitioner took necessary steps to mutate his name in the relevant records of right and applied for mutation of his name before the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 who asked the petitioner to file relevant documents of title in support of his application. Thereafter the petitioner filed an application before the respondent No. 6 on 27-10-1983 with a request to return back the original deed of lease as the vendor of the petitioner made payment of all the dues payable to the House Building Finance Corporation.

6. When the petitioner was pursuing the matter of mutation of his name in the official record of the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 respectively the petitioner came to know, that the case property has already been included in the "Ka" list of the Official Gazette published in the year 1986. Consequentially, the petitioner filed an application under section 7 of The Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance, 1985 ("Ordinance") before, the Court of Settlement with the prayer for deletion of the property of the petitioner from the "Ka" list of abandoned buildings and the same was registered by the respondent No. 3 as Petition Case No. 17 of 1990. The case was taken up for hearing on 4-4-1996 and upon hearing, the Court of Settlement by its Judgment and Order dated 9-4-1996 dismissed the case. At this stage the petitioner moved this court by filing this application under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained this Rule and Order of Stay.

7. By filing a supplementary affidavit the petitioner stating that at the time of filing the writ petition the petitioner could not submit the relevant deed of agreement for sale as the same was not available to him filed the said agreement for sale executed by and between, the original lessee and the petitioner's father Md Akhter Imam Khan on 5-12-1970.

9. The respondent No. 4 Government contested the Rule by filing an Affidavit-in-Opposition contending inter alia that the case property was leased out to one Mojibur Rahman Khan in the year 1960 but that during the War of Liberation in 1971, he left the same uncared for and his whereabouts were not known to the authority. This being the position, the case property assumed the character of an abandoned property under the provisions of PO 16 of 1972. It is contended that the alleged purchase deed and the agreement for sale of 1970 are all fictitious and false documents manufactured for the purpose of grabbing the case property. The Government asserts that the case property was legally enlisted in the "Ka" list of abandoned buildings under the relevant provisions of the Ordinance. The case house being a two-storied building, it is submitted that after such abandonment Provash Chandra Barua, Sanad Kumar Barua and one Abdul Kader were found to be in unauthorized possession of the house and thereafter they were evicted and two disabled freedom fighters namely Manik Chandra Das and Tojammel Haque were given allotment and delivered possession of the property. The petitioner was never in possession of the case property through anybody. It is also asserted that the said evictees, namely, Abdul Kader and SC Barua, as claimants of the case building, filed a case before the Court of Settlement being Case No. 650 of 1988 which was ultimately dismissed.

10. It is further stated that since the house in question is an abandoned property any transfer thereof is barred by law and the petitioner's claim of purchase in the year 1983 is fabricated and false and not sustainable in law and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged.

11. Mr Motiur Rahman learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that pursuant to section 5(1)(a) of the Ordinance no notice was served upon the petitioner and the Government could not show any paper to the effect that the property has on any material date been taken possession of as an abandoned property and in that view of the matter the enlistment of the case property in the "Ka" list of abandoned buildings is ex-facie illegal and without lawful authority. Mr Rahman also submits that the petitioner has been possessing the case property through tenants and, as such, listing of the case property in the 'Ka' list is illegal and erroneous. In support of his submission he has referred to the cases of Begum Lustfunessa vs Bangladesh reported in 42 DLR (AD) 86 and Tarak Chandra Majhi vs Ataher Ali Howlader reported in 8 MLR (AD) 209= 8 BLC (AD) 67. Facts of both the cases are found to be different from the case at hand.

12. It is also argued that the original owner of the case property was all along present in Bangladesh. as a Bangladeshi national and never left this country at any time. It is submitted the original owner was in active control, management and supervision of the property till execution of the deed of agreement of 1970 and also very much present in Bangladesh when the sale deed was executed and registered in the year 1983. Mr Rahman also submits that the Court of Settlement most arbitrarily found the signatures of the original lessee Mojibur Rahman Khan on the lease deed and the kabala dated 25-8-1983 to be different without obtaining a handwriting expert's opinion. He further submits that the Court of Settlement has failed to notice that the agreement for sale was executed by and between the lessee Mojibur Rahman Khan and the petitioner's father since the petitioner was a minor at that time which is also reflected in the recital of the sale deed dated 25-8-1983 given that there was no legal impediment to enter into an agreement for sale by a minor through his legal guardian father. Accordingly, the Judgment and Order of the Court of Settlement is submitted to be a perverse one and liable to be declared illegal and passed without lawful authority.

13. Mr Shahidul Islam, learned l3eputy Attorney-General and Mr Sukumar Biuswas, learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondent No.1 submit that the original lessee Mojibur Rahman Khan left this country during the war of independence in 1971 leaving the case property uncared for and his whereabouts were not known to the authority and, as such, the case property assumed the character of abandoned property and the government took over the possession of the same by evicting unauthorized possessors and allotted the same to two disabled freedom fighters who are in possession of the case property. The case property was legally enlisted in the 'Ka' list of abandoned buildings under the relevant provisions of the Ordinance. They submit that the petitioner or his alleged vendor were never in possession of the case property either before or after PO 16 of 1972 came into force on 28-2-1972. It is also argued that the Court of Settlement rightly found that the signatures of Mojibur Rahman Khan on the lease deed and the sale deed of 1983 differ from each other. Learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that the agreement for sale of 1970 filed in Court by a supplementary affidavit clearly shows that it is an ante dated agreement manufactured by the petitioner very recently by interpolation and fabrication and for that reason the petitioner did not and could not file it before the Court of Settlement at the time of filing the application under section 7 of the Ordinance and also at the time of hearing of the case.

14. It is also argued that the Court of Settlement has rightly observed in its Judgment and Order that the petitioner utterly failed to prove his case by submitting relevant documents before it or indeed by otherwise establishing the presence of the original lessee Mojibur Rahman Khan in this country on or before PO 16 of 1972 came into force (i.e. during the relevant period) and his possession of the case property and the evidence of such possession i.e payment of any bill for that period. Mr Islam also submits that no evidence was adduced by the petitioner in the Court of Settlement that his vendor Mojibur Rahman occupied, managed or supervised the case property or he himself was in possession and management of the case property on the relevant date (i.e. 28-2-1972) to prove that the said property is not an abandoned property. To back up this submission, he draws our attention to the cases of Rowshan Ara Begum vs Secretary, Ministry of Works reported in 59 DLR (AD) 165 and Golam Rabbani vs Chairman, Court of Settlement reported in 13 MLR (AD) 345 = 61 DLR (AD) 15.

15. Mr Islam also argued that the petitioner has failed to produce any papers and documents before the Court of Settlement as well as before this Court to substantiate his claim that the vendor was present in Bangladesh and he managed and supervised the case property on 28-2-1972 or thereafter, and that the present petitioner by virtue of any deed has been managing, supervising or possessing the property. Given this scenario, he argues the abandoned character of the property remains unrequited,

16. It is also argued that this Court is not a court of appeal and it cannot interfere with the findings of a court of facts under its Writ Jurisdiction unless it can be shown that the Court of Settlement has acted without jurisdiction or made any finding upon no evidence or without considering any material facts causing prejudiced to the petitioner or it has acted malafide or in violation of the principles of natural justice. In support of this submission, he has referred to the case of Bangladesh vs Md Jalil, reported in 49 DLR (AD) 26 =15 BLD (AD) 175.

17. He further submits that the list published under section 5(2) of the ordinance is conclusive and the government has no obligation either to deny the fact alleged or to disclose the basis of treating the property as abandoned property. It is for the claimant to prove that the property is not an abandoned property.

18. Mr Islam also submits that the paramount issue to be decided in this case is whether the original owner Mojibur Rahman Khan at the relevant time was present in Bangladesh and not the validity of the alleged sale deed of 1983. It is asserted in this regard that the petitioner failed to establish that his vendor was present in Bangladesh at the relevant time and managed and supervised the property in question in person.

19. Heard the learned Advocates for the parties, perused the writ petition, supplementary affidavit, affidavit-in-opposition and the annexures annexed thereto as well as the records called for from the Court of Settlement by this Court.

20. Before discussing the merit of the case and going through the impugned Judgment of the Court of Settlement, at the very outset we are to look into the scope and jurisdiction of this Court to interfere with the Judgment passed by the Court of Settlement.

21. The High Court Division exercising power under Article 102 of the Constitution is not necessarily to sit on appeal on the Judgment and Order of the Court of Settlement as a court of appeal and, as such, this Court is not required to make a determination of facts on its own. The scope and objective and exercise of jurisdiction has been clearly spelt out by the Appellate Division in the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Md Jalil reported in 15 BLD (AD) 175 = 49 DLR (AD) 26 limiting intervention under Article 102 of the Constitution in the cases where the Court of Settlement's finding may be said to have been based on no evidence or the Court proceeded upon non-consideration of material evidence or facts or where the Court of Settlement may be found to have acted mala fide or in violation of the principles of natural justice, thereby contributing to a scenario where the Court of Settlement may be found to have acted without jurisdiction.

<u>22. Section 5(2) of the Ordinance clearly provides that the list published under Sub-section (1) shall be conclusive evidence of the fact that the buildings included therein are abandoned properties and have been vested in the Government as such. Section 7 says that a person claiming any right or interest in any such building may make an application to the Court of Settlement for exclusion of the building from such list on the ground that the building is not an abandoned property and has not been vested in the Government under PO 16 of 1972 or that his right or interest in the building has not been affected by the provisions of the Order. The onus, therefore, is on the claimant to prove that the building is not an abandoned property. The Government has no obligation either to deny the fact alleged by the claimant or to disclose the basis of treating the property as abandoned property merely because the same is disputed by the claimant.</u>

23. The property in question is a 'Ka' listed property and admittedly not in the possession of the claimant but in the possession of the Government through its DN holder, namely, Manik Chandra Das and Tojammel Haque. Though the petitioner-claimant claimed that he purchased the property from the original lessee Mr Mojibur Rahman Khan by a deed of sale executed and registered on 28-5-1983 pursuance to an agreement alleged to have been entered into between the petitioner and the said original lessee Mr Mojibur gahman Khan on 5-12-1970 and also claimed that he has been possessing the case property since execution of the agreement for sale through tenants, namely, SC Barua and SK Barua, it appears that the said SC Barua and one Abdul Kader filed another case being No. 650 of 1988 before the Court of Settlement as claimants of the property which was ultimately dismissed. Moreover, the alleged tenants of the petitioner did not come forward to depose in favour of the petitioner's case before the Court of Settlement to substantiate the petitioner's claim. The petitioner claimed that he purchased the property on the basis of an agreement of 1970, but the said agreement for sale was not produced before the Court of Settlement at the time of filing application even at the time of hearing of the case. The said agreement of the year 1970 has been filed in this Court for the first time by a supplementary affidavit dated 8-6-2014 at the fag end of the hearing of this Rule.

24. From a perusal of the impugned Judgment of the Court of Settlement it appears that the Court found it difficult to accept the contention of the petitioner that the signatures of Mojibur Rahman appearing in the lease deed and the signatures appearing in the sale deed of 1983 are same. Additionally, it also appears to this Court that signatures contained on the agreement (Annexure-Z), sale deed dated 25-8-1983 (Annexure-C), Original sale agreement dated 29-7-1960 ( Annexure-B), General Power of Attorney dated 21-5-1972 (Annexure-D), Deed of revocation of power of attorney dated 25-8-1983 (Annexure-A), Affidavit of Mojibur Rahman Khan dated 15-11-1983 (Annexure-W), differ from each other and particularly with the signature contained in the lease agreement of 1960. Moreover, the agreement for sale (Annexure-Z) apparently seems to be very recently written and or typed on stamp and cartridge paper and it also appears that the endorsement on the reverse of the stamp paper used in the agreement is a product of interpolation in that the name of Mojibur Rahman Khan endorsed as the purchaser of the same (known as "যন্ত্রীক") has been written by erasing someone's name and the writing thereof acknowledging receipt of subsequent part payment on different dates by Mojibur Rahman Khan and signature of the parties to the said agreement also seem to be very recently inked by the same pen. Besides, no explanation has been forthcoming from petitioner's side as to why the sale deed has been executed and registered after a long period of 13 years of execution of the alleged agreement for sale and why the original documents were not handed over to the petitioner at the time of execution of the agreement by said Mojibur Rahman Khan and for what reason PC Barua has been appointed as Attorney of Mojibur Rahman in the year 1972 after execution of an agreement for sale on 5-12-1970 and delivery of the possession by said Mojibur Rahman to the petitioner. It is also noted that, the petitioner could not produce even a single scrap of paper showing the presence of Mojibur Rahman Khan in Bangladesh at the relevant time when PO 16 of 1972 came into force on 28-2-1972 and thereafter until 1983. Moreover, the petitioner indeed failed to produce the said Mojibur Rahman Khan before the Court of Settlement at the time of hearing of the case as otherwise asked by the Court and also to furnish khan's address before me Court of Settlement to ascertain the truth. Non-production of the original owner Mojibur Rahman Khan before the Court in spite of the petitioner's assertion that he is very much present in Bangladesh, has in this Court's view made the claim of the petitioner about the presence of Mojibur Rahman Khan in Bangladesh and execution of the agreement for sale and the sale deed highly questionable and created doubt about the identity of said Mojibur Rahman Khan, thereby, seriously weakening the case of the petitioner. Notably, the non-production of any document/evidence in support of management, control and supervision of the property by the vendor or the petitioner himself and non-appearance of the original lessee before the Court of Settlement proves that the owner was not present in Bangladesh at the relevant time and he left the property uncared for. The anomalies in the documents as stated above have also, indeed, made the entire case of the petitioner questionable. In other words the documents, the petitioner could produce to substantiate his claim before the Court of Settlement are dated after the date of alleged purchase. But the petitioner could not produce any evidence to establish that the owner was present in Bangladesh at the relevant time when PO 16 of 1972 came into force and that he managed, possessed or controlled the property in person. It is also noted that by an affidavit sworn by Mojibur Rahman Khan before the Notary Public on 15-11-1983 he claimed that he has been possessing the case property peacefully and without any interference from any quarter and within the knowledge of all concerned from the date of lease deed of 1960 which contradicts the statement made in the agreement for sale of 1970 and subsequent story of possessing the property by the petitioner through tenants.

25. This Court also notes, that the Court of Settlement as it appears from the impugned Judgment has considered the crucial point as to whether the petitioner has been able to rebut the position taken by the respondent Government that the said Mojibur Rahman Khan was not present in Bangladesh and his whereabouts were not known on 28-2-1972, i.e., the date when PO 16 of 1972 came into force. The petitioner, therefore, at material times during the Settlement Court proceedings was under an obligation to rebut the presumption under section 5(2) of the Ordinance. The Court of Settlement categorically found, upon considering the documentary evidence on record that the petitioner not Only failed to prove that Mojibur Rahman Khan was indeed present in Bangladesh but were far less able to prove that his claim of title to the property in question was immuned from the perilous effect of PO 16 of 1972.

26. The Court of Settlement in the present case not only disbelieved the claim of the petitioner as to the presence of Mojibur Rahman Khan in Bangladesh up to 1983, or at any relevant time leading to that date, but also disbelieved the story of execution of agreement for sale in favour of a minor and execution of a sale deed on 25-8-1983 in favour of the petitioner in its entirety. Inconsistencies in the documents as to the petitioner's possession of the property in question through his vendor as well as his tenants were pointed out by the Court of Settlement in its Judgment and those inconsistencies compelled that Court to take an adverse view against the petitioner's case. It was also clearly held that the petitioner crucially failed to prove that said Mojibur Rahman Khan was present in Bangladesh on 28-2-1972 or that he was in possession, management and control of the property in question before and after 28-2-1972 i.e., on the date when the PO 16 of 1972 came into force.

27. This Court has perused the contents of the impugned Judgment and Order of 9-4-1996 passed by the Settlement Court. As apparent from the text of the Judgment itself and as substantiated by additional reference to the records of the Court of Settlement as called for and made available to this Court, the Court of Settlement was mindful of stating both that the claimant before it took no needful steps to prove his claim and to produce the original lessee Mojibur Rahman Khan. That lapse appears most blatantly in the facts and circumstances of this case. It is also noted that the papers and documents produced by the petitioner before this Court do not confirm the presence of Mojibur Rahman Khan at all material times. Given this Court's understanding it is found that the Court of Settlement properly appreciated the fact that the claimant petitioner could not duly discharge his onus of proving his case independently of the Government and that in doing so he failed to establish a continuous scenario of active ownership, occupation, supervision and management of the case property both before and after the promulgation of PO 16 of 1972.

28. By that reason and confining this Court's scrutiny to the objective of finding whether the impugned Judgment is perverse or not, this Court has inevitably arrived at the conclusion that the Court of Settlement's impugned Judgment and Order of 9-4-1996 suffers from no illegality and, as such, this Court finds itself wholly disinclined to interfere with the Judgment of the Court of Settlement as otherwise prayed for in this Writ Petition.

29. Accordingly, this Court finds no merit in the Application and no substance in the Rule Nisi issued warranting interference by this Court.

30. In the result, the Rule is, hereby, discharged without any order as to costs.

31. The Order of Stay as initially granted is, hereby, recalled and vacated.

32. Send down the records received from the First Court of Settlement, Segunbagicha, PS Ramna, Dhaka, forthwith along with a copy of this Judgment.

The petitioner is permitted to take back the original documents subject to furnishing the visible photocopies of the same, particularly all the back pages of the agreement for sale dated 5-12-1970 (Annexure-Z) to the supplementary affidavit on condition of refilling the same as and when asked for.

End.
